sections.content:
301,090 people

were counted on the census as "customer service occupations (other)" in England and Wales in March 2021.
People who do this type of work have a variety of customer service occupations not elsewhere classified.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "customer service occupations (other)", 17.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "customer service occupations (other)" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "customer service occupations (other)" included:

  • early education and childcare assistants
  • tyre, exhaust and windscreen fitters
  • telephone salespersons

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "customer service occupations (other)" there were more women than men (65.2% compared with 34.8%).

This means "customer service occupations (other)" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "customer service occupations".

Men made up 34.8% and women made up 65.2% of "customer service occupations (other)"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "customer service occupations (other)" included:

  • kitchen and catering assistants
  • education advisers and school inspectors
  • archivists, conservators and curators

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "customer service occupations (other)" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "customer service occupations (other)" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "customer service occupations (other)", 13.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (67.3% compared with 32.7%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98.7%) than self-employed (1.3%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
